aspects.says: A dependency taken through the constructor is a compile error when the wiring forgets it, and requireNonNull refuses a null at construction; a service locator lookup fails only at the first request that needs it.
basis: section:A Constructor Parameter Turns a Forgotten Dependency Into a Compile Error

aspects.says: A test with a fake checks the outcome and survives a refactor that changes the calls; a mock test that verifies calls fails it although no decision changed.
basis: section:A Fake Checks the Outcome; a Mock Checks the Calls

aspects.says: Iterating a ServiceLoader constructs each provider it passes, so one that can't start fails the lookup; stream() with Provider.type() chooses without constructing, and load(type, loader) looks where it is told instead of the context class loader.
basis: section:Iterating the Loader Builds Every Provider Before the One You Want

aspects.says: A policy that constructs its own detail can't be built, and so can't be tested, without that detail; taking an interface through the constructor lets a test pass a fake.
basis: section:A Policy That Builds Its Own Mailer Can't Run Without a Mail Server

aspects.says: Injecting an interface that the detail's jar declares is injection without inversion: the policy still can't compile without that jar; the interface belongs in the policy's package, in its terms.
basis: section:The Interface Belongs to the Policy, So the Policy Compiles Without the Mail Code

aspects.says: ServiceLoader finds class-path providers only through META-INF/services/<interface name>; a provider class on the class path without that file is not found.
basis: section:ServiceLoader Picks the Implementation From the Class Path
